title: Rapid prototype SDK hackbench notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working-pad for a small, reusable "hackbench" flow aimed at enabling engineers and product partners to move from idea -> measurable prototype with Redwood SDKs in under 60 minutes. This doc captures the lightweight steps, shortcuts, example snippets, observability checks, and TODOs from the January sprint. Not a final spec; intended to be minimal, pragmatic, and easily copy/pastable into demo repos.

Outcomes we target from a single hackbench run:
- App-level prototype (chat or summarization widget) wired to Redwood hosted API or local dev runner
- Basic telemetry: token counts, latency per request, error snapshots, and one quality metric (ROUGE / human score placeholder)
- One togglable optimization: enable prefix-caching or switch quantized model -> measure delta
- README that a newcomer can follow in ~45-60 minutes

Audience:
- Product PM or Solutions SE validating an integration pattern
- Frontend or full-stack engineer who needs a quick proof of concept
- Developer advocates building short workshops or office-hours labs

High-level constraints and choices:
- Default to hosted API for fastest onboarding, but include an alternative path that uses the local CLI-runner for disconnected/private demos.
- Keep dependency surface small: Node + one small web UI or Python Flask for backend examples.
- Use the SDK patterns we want to promote: ephemeral keys, streaming responses for UX, explicit telemetry hooks.
- Opt for pragmatic code snippets instead of fully polished apps.

Quickstart blueprint (60-minute path)
1) Prep (5-10 min)
- Fork the hackbench template repo: GHP-RI/hackbench-template -> clone
- Create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY (note: use ephemeral demo key, instructions in README)
- Install: npm ci or pip install -r requirements.txt

2) Run a minimal server (5 min)
- Node/express example: node server/index.js (server listens on 3000)
- CLI-runner alternative: ./tools/cli-runner start --model=redwood-small --port=8080 (use for private demos)

3) Wire simple widget (10-15 min)
- frontend: minimal HTML + fetch POST /api/generate with a prompt
- backend: call SDK client generate with streaming response, forward chunks to frontend using SSE or websockets for smooth typing UI

Example backend snippet (Node, minimal):
- const { Redwood } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
- const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
- app.post('/api/generate', async (req, res) => {
    const prompt = req.body.prompt;
    const stream = await client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-chat-v1', input: prompt });
    stream.on('data', chunk => res.write(chunk));
    stream.on('end', () => res.end());
    stream.on('error', (e) => { console.error(e); res.status(500).send('err'); });
  });

Notes: SDK names above are illustrative; use stable client method names from the SDK reference. Keep error handling short but include telemetry hooks (below).

4) Telemetry quick check (10 min)
- Add a single stats endpoint that logs: tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, http_latency_ms, model_version
- Example: increment simple in-memory counters and print to console for demo. For more realism, ship to existing telemetry ingestion: GHP-RI/telemetry/logstash-demo.
- Sample payload we collect: { request_id, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, model, success }

5) Micro-optimization toggle (10-15 min)
- Provide two routes or a query param: ?opt=cache or ?opt=quant
- Implementation idea: when ?opt=cache -> attach a prefixCache key generated from prompt namespace and check before generate(); when ?opt=quant -> call model variant 'redwood-chat-v1-quant'
- Measure delta: run N=10 requests and record mean latency and tokens used. Log to console and/or produce a small CSV report.

6) Quality quick check (5 min)
- For summarization flows, use a small evaluation harness: run 5 canonical prompts and compare outputs to gold answers. Compute a naive match rate or token-overlap score. This is just to show tradeoffs when switching optimizations.

Developer-facing artifacts produced
- README.md with step-by-step run instructions and where to edit sample prompts
- demo-recording.gif (30s) showing streaming UI and console telemetry log
- results.csv with latency/tokens for baseline vs optimization
- tiny checklist visible in the repo: "what to demo" (latency, streaming, telemetry, fallback)

Telem & observability details (practical minimal set)
- Hook: client.onRequestComplete((meta) => sendTelemetry({ request_id: meta.id, tokens: meta.tokens, model: meta.model, latency: meta.latency }))
- If using CLI-runner local mode, add a /metrics endpoint that emits Prometheus-friendly counters for simple scraping in a workshop environment.
- Error snapshots: capture request_id + error stack + last 512 bytes of model output in a local file for review.

UX and workshop notes (for the person running the session)
- Start by showing how streaming feels vs single response: ask the audience which one feels faster and why.
- Show telemetry console while you change the opt toggle. Audience should observe immediate delta in latency/compute.
- Keep a small script of failure modes: 401 with ephemeral key, local runner port conflict, CORS on demo page — quick fixes documented in README.

Unresolved questions / decisions (work in progress)
- Which model names should be used in template to minimize churn when we rename models? Consider a stable alias layer (e.g., redwood/demo-chat).
- How much infra do we provide in the template? Full Docker compose for local runner vs single binary start. Tradeoff: reproducibility vs friction.
- Default telemetry backend for demos: stdout vs real ingestion. Provide both but make stdout the default.

Quick checklist for finaling the template before promotion:
- [ ] Add ephemeral key generation script for workshop hosts
- [ ] Include small dataset (5 prompts + gold) for quality checks
- [ ] Add a one-click run script that seeds env and launches browser tab
- [ ] Add license and contributor notes
- [ ] Document privacy notes if attendees paste real data

Follow-ups and ownership:
- Action: Priya to spin up the minimal Docker compose for CLI-runner by 2026-03-10 (JIRA-RI-4321)
- Action: Noah to draft a 10-minute workshop script and 3-slide intro to streaming vs batch by 2026-03-05
- Action: Ava to add ephemeral-key helper and update README by 2026-03-02

Appendix: short troubleshooting cheats (notes-to-self)
- If streaming stops mid-response: check connection idle timeout (nginx/proxy). Bump keepalive to 120s.
- If local CLI-runner reports GPU OOM: switch to cpu-mode or choose smaller model alias.
- If demo page shows CORS errors: make sure server adds header Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for the workshop network.

Minimal README excerpt to include in repo (copy/paste-ready):
- Step 1: git clone && npm ci
- Step 2: cp .env.example .env and add REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Step 3: npm run start or ./tools/cli-runner start --model=redwood-demo-chat
- Step 4: open http://localhost:3000 and type a prompt
- Step 5: flip ?opt=cache in the UI and re-run the same prompt to observe difference in console telemetry

End of notes.
